wader.text: It stares into the mud with the confidence of a bird who has never once been wrong about worms.

toll_ghost.text: Twenty-three years in that booth. 'Seventy pence, please, ta.' Now it's free and I've nothing to say to people.
They put a plaque up when the tolls ended. It says 'thank you'. I take it personally.

mud_watcher.text: The Severn estuary hosts tens of thousands of wading birds in winter: dunlin, redshank, curlew, the lot.
The mud looks like nothing. It's actually a five-star buffet. Mind your boots.

bridge_cyclist.text: It's over a mile of bridge. You can run it. The wind does half the work and half the swearing.
In a gale they close it to high-sided lorries. In a bad gale, to me. I've been refused entry twice.

sailor_sev.text: The Severn bore is a wave that rolls up the river on big spring tides. Surfers ride it for miles.
My job is to avoid it. The surfers' job is the reverse. We nod politely.

motorist.text: Two countries in two minutes. You'd think the sat-nav would say something. Mine says 'recalculating'.
Service station on the English side. I had a pasty. It was not a Cornish one. I checked.
